basics.name: Ricardo Orellana
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer
basics.summary: I’m Ricardo, a software engineer in Guadalajara, Mexico. I turn complex problems into software that feels simple. Since 2015, I’ve built mobile apps, trading platforms, and the systems behind them. These days, I’m a Senior Software Engineer at Change.org. I like understanding the problem, working closely with people, and leaving the code a little easier to work with.

work.name: Change.org
work.summary: I’m working on tools that help people speak up about the things they care about. At Change.org, that means helping turn a personal concern into a petition, a conversation, and a chance to make something happen.
highlights: Focus: civic tech, web platform, product

work.name: ARCOS LLC
work.summary: I worked across the frontend and backend of the ARCOS platform. A lot of the job was connecting the pieces: building features, keeping the application responsive, and making sure it could grow without getting harder to use.

work.name: Bitso
work.summary: I helped bring new features from an idea to a release, working with product, design, mobile, and backend teams. Along the way, I helped shape the tech stack and mentored React developers, sharing patterns that made everyday work easier.
highlights: Cross-functional planning with product, design, mobile, and backend

work.name: EPAM Systems Mexico
work.summary: I built and maintained software across client projects, with a focus on code other engineers could understand and test. I also planned delivery, documented technical decisions, and helped teammates work through tricky implementation details.
highlights: Testable software built on clean code and SOLID principles
Documented technical decisions and planned delivery
Unblocked engineers on implementation challenges across projects

work.name: Rever Inc.
work.summary: I led development across the frontend and backend, and introduced microservices as the platform grew. I also looked after development, staging, and production, adding automation, monitoring, and logging so we could see what was happening and keep things running.
highlights: Ran development, staging, and production environments with automation, monitoring, and logging

work.name: Propelics
work.summary: This is where I got my start: building apps for iOS, Android, and mobile web with JavaScript and Appcelerator Titanium. Moving between platforms taught me to follow a bug carefully, pay attention to performance, and think about the person on the other side of the screen.
highlights: Shipped for iOS, Android, and mobile web
Traced bugs and resolved cross-platform performance issues

projects.name: Bitso Exchanger
projects.description: I contributed to a cryptocurrency exchange that helps people buy and sell digital assets. The goal: make a complicated financial product feel straightforward to use.

projects.name: Power E*TRADE
projects.description: A trading platform that brings stocks, options, and futures together. I contributed to a product where a clear interface matters when there’s a lot to keep track of.

projects.name: Continuous Improvement
projects.description: A web and mobile app that gives manufacturing employees a place to share ideas and improve the way they work. Practical tools for the people closest to the problem.

projects.name: Apple Financial Services
projects.description: A mobile app for putting together quotes for Apple products. It brought an enterprise workflow onto a smaller screen, where clarity and ease of use matter even more.

projects.name: Audithere
projects.description: A mobile app for auditing items. One of my early projects, and a chance to turn a hands-on process into something people could carry in their pocket.

meta.note: Project dates follow the project timeline and may differ from employment dates.
